candidates.tagline: Coca-Cola redesigned Coke Zero to look more like Coke. Now nobody can tell them apart.
candidates.story: In July 2026, Coca-Cola's global 'unified look' rebrand made Coke Zero predominantly red with the classic Coca-Cola logo — so similar to regular Coke that a Melbourne flight attendant's TikTok about repeatedly handing out the wrong drink went viral with 850,000 views, and people with diabetes and allergies raised safety concerns; Creative Bloq reported the confusion was 'still happening three months on' in October.
candidates.why_funny: The company spent decades making Coke Zero unmistakably black so nobody would grab the wrong one, then decided 'unified branding' was more important than the ability to tell the sugar-free version apart from the full-sugar one.
candidates.alt: A refrigerator shelf packed with identical-looking red Coca-Cola cans, with only faint 'NO SUGAR' text visible at the top of some cans in the back row — all otherwise indistinguishable at a glance

candidates.tagline: Nothing's CMF built a $109 Bluetooth speaker. Every tech outlet called it a milk carton.
candidates.story: CMF by Nothing launched its first-ever Bluetooth speakers on October 12, 2026 — the Speaker S ($59) and Speaker M ($109) — with a boxy rectangular design and gabled top so similar to dairy packaging that TechRadar, Yanko Design, and Business Today all independently led with the milk-carton comparison in their headlines.
candidates.why_funny: The entire press corps covering a premium audio launch independently agreed the design looked like something you'd find next to the 2% milk — and CMF apparently considers this a selling point.
candidates.alt: Four CMF by Nothing Bluetooth speakers in white, orange, dark grey, and turquoise arranged together, each with a large circular speaker grille and small volume knob — their boxy rectangular shapes resembling milk cartons
candidates.credit: CMF by Nothing / Business Today India
